Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our security and ops side:

1) PHI: Veridian will be handling PHI in the initial integration, so HIPAA controls are required. We can share the high-level data classification doc but legal will want to see any encryption and access controls you enforce.
2) Logs: our compliance team typically asks for 1 year of audit/system logs retained online and 3 years available for e-discovery (archived). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports a 1yr hot retention + archived tier to satisfy e-discovery?
3) Backups: standard expectation is 90 days of regular backups retained, with the option to keep long-term snapshots for up to 7 years on request (charged). Do you have a separate backup retention SLA?
4) Encryption/KMS: are keys customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed? If Redwood-managed, can you provide details on HSM/KMS provider and key rotation policy?

Also: please attach your SOC 2 readiness summary; legal will review and advise if they need the final report or just the attestation.

Thanks —
Sam

Sam —

Quick answers to your bullets so legal/ops have something concrete for review:

- SOC 2: Redwood is in the final stages of SOC 2 Type II and expects completion by Q4 2028. In the meantime we can share a SOC 2 readiness summary and sample control evidence (link below). If Veridian requires a completed Type II report before go-live, let's flag that now and we can discuss interim compensating controls.
- Log retention: Redwood supports configurable retention policies. Typical default config for enterprise customers: 90 days of hot/fast-access audit logs, 1 year of standard retention (searchable), and optional archival to cold storage for multi-year e-discovery (up to 7 years). We can map retention tiers to Veridian's e-discovery needs and provide an export on request.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are retained separately from logs. Default SLA: 90-day snapshot retention (restore points daily), with the ability to extend to custom retention windows (paid add-on). Snapshots are immutable once written; deletion requests follow a documented erase workflow with an auditable deletion log.
- Encryption/KMS: we support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer BYOK via AWS KMS or GCP KMS. Production keys used for at-rest encryption are HSM-backed; key rotation policy is 90 days for data-plane keys, vault keys per customer are configurable.

I've attached a short summary that covers the items above. Jonas will follow up with a prefilled questionnaire to speed your review.
